scientific_integrity.limitations: No arbitrary phase shifts, no general n>=3 extremal classification, and no optimal two-frequency formula for radii below 1/5. Finite arithmetic checks are supplementary.
scientific_integrity.motivation: Recent cosine-sign-correlation literature; later continuous-threshold literature is explicitly compared, not treated as the earliest motivating public source.
scientific_integrity.priority_risk: Earlier unindexed folklore about interval-intersection radius scaling may exist. Previously determined reciprocal-radius two-frequency value is explicitly used as prior coverage, not claimed new.
scientific_integrity.proof: Finite interval-center decomposition and concavity of normalized overlap, sharp powers-of-three equality family, independent exact finite arithmetic for reciprocal radius 1/5, full nonreciprocal interval interpolation.
scientific_integrity.scope: Any finite nonempty collection of unshifted positive integer frequencies, any continuous even strictly decreasing antipodal wave, and threshold radii 0<r<=s<=1/4.

title: Sharp radius scaling for simultaneous Fourier-threshold correlations
